body.objective: Prevent resident agents from interpreting `s-f work ready --stream S` returning zero as an empty queue when that agent already holds a live exclusive assignment in the same stream.
body.stop_condition: Add an agent-aware readiness surface, either `s-f work ready --stream S --agent A` or equivalent use of the declared SF_AGENT identity. If A holds a live exclusive lease, print that item first with state, lease epoch, checkpoint status, expiry and the exact `work-package`/`work show` command, then list additional pullable work separately. A zero pullable count must say `0 additional pullable; current assignment: I`, never merely `0 ready`. `work pull --agent A` must likewise refuse a second item while naming the held lease and recovery command. Preserve stream-only coordinator semantics when no agent is supplied. Add deterministic fixtures for: one held lease plus zero additional ready; one held lease plus another ready item; LEASED-UNSTARTED; checkpointed current lease; expired/released lease; same item after yield; and two streams using the same human-readable title but distinct stable agent IDs. Reproduce the 2026-07-21 Classical and Quantum cases where overview showed valid live leases while the resident windows concluded `no new work item is currently ready to pull` and stopped.
body.forbid: no automatic lease release or task switch; no second exclusive acquisition; no inference of agent identity from terminal title alone; no conflation of active assignment with READY queue depth; no treating absent heartbeat as scientific idleness; no physics-specific item names in implementation
notes: Current recovery requires a manually authored inbox request telling the agent not to pull again and to render its already-held package. The launcher should make this the normal first-class path.

This composes with science-forge-resident-await-and-wakeup and the programme-level one-live-exclusive-per-agent CAS request; it is specifically the misleading read-only UX that leaves valid leases unconsumed.
